name: Dumbbell Step-Up
cues: Plant your whole foot on the box
Drive up through the top leg without pushing off the bottom foot
Stand fully tall on the box before stepping down
Lower yourself under control with the same leg

qa.note: Approved by the owner 2026-10-01 (bulk approval of every pending exercise). Earlier findings, kept for follow-up: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. review: Rebuilt. The old loop was physically wrong: the centre of mass sat up to 20 cm behind the box foot while the trailing foot was in the air, it stood on one leg with the centre of mass 12 cm off the foot, and the rear foot took 70% of the weight at the bottom, which contradicts the cue. Now both feet stand on the box at the top, the weight shifts over the box foot before the trailing foot leaves (and back after it lands), and the step down is a controlled single-leg lowering with the foot on its ball at touch-down. For the owner: from the front, the box knee sits a few cm outside the foot line at the bottom, because the hip must sit outside the foot and the rig has no tibial rotation. The trailing foot also needs a new 35 mm floor tolerance. | skeptic: The movement shape is right (both feet on the box at the top, weight shifts before lift-off, controlled single-leg lowering, side sheet clean), but three points need the owner, and the report is inaccurate on one of them. (1) At the bottom (frames 66-68) the trailing foot is flat on the floor, with the heel at 0-1 mm. COP is at (-24, 37) mm against the box midfoot (-100, z 160) and the trailing midfoot (95, z -220). That puts about 32-39% of the weight on the bottom foot, not the reported 25%. The first 0.3 s of the concentric (frames 69-78) is a weight transfer off that planted foot, which sits uneasily with the cue 'without pushing off the bottom foot'. (2) The box knee ends 71 mm outside the heel-to-ball line at frame 66 (knee x -176, foot line x -105), while COP is on the medial half of the box foot (x -65, foot centre -100). From the front this reads as the knee pushed out.
